answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Signed orienteering club membership with orienteering federation attestation changes that arithmetic: a membership the federation kept across years of courses, so the nebula for each fake is paid in the real world. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the vertex of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The garden is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
